name: When does water-damaged drywall need full replacement instead of a patch?

mainEntity.name: When does water-damaged drywall need full replacement instead of a patch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water-damaged drywall must be cut out and replaced if it is soft, sagging, discolored, or crumbling. Once drywall core gypsum absorbs moisture, it loses structural strength and can harbor hidden mold behind the wall cavity. Before cutting into the wall, verify that the plumbing or roof leak is completely resolved and the wall cavity has dried out. When Abraham Becerra and the HH Remodeling crew step in, we cut out the damaged sheetrock back to solid studs, inspect the interior framing and insulation, hang moisture-resistant board where appropriate, and blend textures across the entire span to ensure structural integrity and a clean finish.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall must be replaced if it has softened, sagged, or stayed damp, as gypsum loses strength and harbors mold. Small, dry surface stains can sometimes be sealed and patched.
